$comment: Capability registry — the single source of truth for what each security/reliability capability of ApexMail ACTUALLY is, versus what the marketing/compliance surfaces say about it. Companion to docs/development/topology-manifest.json (which owns runtime topology; this file owns capability truth). tools/check_capability_claims.py proves: (a) every entry at stage >= runtime-wired has evidence that EXISTS in the tree — docker_target present in BOTH the Dockerfile (FROM runtime-base AS <target>) and topology-manifest.json, compose_service present in the compose files, and evidence.env_gate.name greppable in the wiring crate's Rust sources (null env_gate = always-on wiring, allowed); (b) the claim surfaces (marketing security/architecture pages + compliance templates) may NAME a sub-runtime-wired capability (stage < runtime-wired) only inside explicit [roadmap]-marked context — every scan_aliases hit outside that context on a surface is a claim that the capability must be at stage >= runtime-wired or the gate FAILS (advertised == deployed, both directions driven by the per-capability alias lists below); (c) crate README wiring-status lines match registry stages: stage >= runtime-wired forbids a 'NOT WIRED INTO PRODUCTION' banner (unless a stale_marker_exceptions needle still proves the banner stale) and requires the env-gate name to appear in the README when one is declared; stage < runtime-wired requires the banner or an explicit 'wiring in flight' statement; (d) registry self-consistency: every entry carries exactly ONE lifecycle state — its `stage` — so retired-state language ('not landed', 'unlanded', 'wiring in flight', 'not wired', 'no caller') anywhere in an entry's own text is a failure, as is any wording that contradicts the entry's stage (library-only/unwired language on a stage >= runtime-wired entry), and an in_flight_wiring item whose env gate is already greppable in the tree (a landed item must be removed and its stage raised in the same change). Strictness: CAPABILITY_GATE_STRICT=0 (default) prints genuinely-unlanded in-flight wiring items as WARN and exits 0; =1 fails on them. The in_flight_wiring list is empty today — the 2026-09 wiring wave landed.

stage_rules.implemented: code exists; nothing consumes it outside its own crate
stage_rules.integration-tested: consumed by crates/{integration-tests,fuzz-tests,perf-tests,load-tests} only — zero production call path
stage_rules.runtime-wired: a production binary constructs/mounts it in a live request or delivery path (monitor/flag-gated counts — say so in evidence)
stage_rules.deployed: runtime-wired AND running in the prod compose topology with default-on behavior
stage_rules.monitored: deployed AND covered by an alerting rule / dashboard in deploy/
stage_rules.advertised: deployed+monitored truthfully AND the marketing claim matches the wired behavior — only this stage may be named in claim surfaces outside [roadmap] context

scan.context_rule: A capability alias may appear on a claim surface only (1) on a line that itself contains the marker, or (2) anywhere between a marker line and the next markdown heading (line starting with '#') or the marker_close line. Markdown ATX headings are not scanned (they organize; they do not claim). Everything else is a bare capability-name drop: it requires the named capability at stage >= runtime-wired and FAILS the gate otherwise. Limitation (by design): the gate can only police the capability names enumerated in scan_aliases below — a NEW product claim about a capability that has no alias entry is invisible to it, so every new security/reliability claim must add its alias here in the same change.
scan.word_boundary_tokens: aliases shorter than 5 chars or all-caps acronyms are matched with word boundaries (\b) so 'SSO' does not hit inside longer words; phrase aliases are matched as case-insensitive substrings.

in_flight_wiring.$comment: Wiring contracts agreed with a crate owner whose code has not arrived in the tree yet. The checker FAILS (both modes) on an item whose env gate is already greppable in the wiring crate's Rust sources: a landed item must be REMOVED from this list in the same change that raises the capability entry's stage, so the registry never carries two lifecycle states for one capability. Each entry names the env gate that WILL gate the wiring so registry/gate/READMEs agree on the contract before the code arrives.

stale_marker_exceptions.$comment: crates/*/README.md markers that are STALE relative to the dep graph (the crate IS consumed by a production binary). Each exception carries <file>:<needle> pairs that the checker greps — if the wiring disappears (or the crate owner fixes the README marker), the exception goes stale and the checker FAILS, forcing this registry to be re-triaged. Crates are owned by the mail-server agents; this registry may not edit their READMEs.
